objective: Explain generic database read/write separation and bounded failover roles without claiming transparent consistency or automatic correctness.

confirmed: A primary role accepts writes while read-only replicas may serve read traffic.
Changes flow from the primary role toward read-only replicas through a generic synchronization relationship.
A failover decision requires observing role health and selecting a valid replacement role.
simplifications: Show one write entrance, one primary role, two representative read-only replicas, one read entrance, and one compact failover decision zone.
Treat synchronization and failover as generic responsibilities rather than a vendor-specific algorithm.
blocked: Do not claim zero data loss, instant failover, perfect consistency, unlimited reads, or automatic correctness.
Do not add vendor names, protocols, latency numbers, throughput numbers, regions, consensus nodes, or extra storage roles.
Do not connect the failover note to any node. Do not draw replica-to-query arrows. No extra copy beyond exact_text.

invariants: No response arrows are shown. Query arrows point FROM query TO replicas.
Failover is an unconnected explanatory note, not a topology transition.

composition.structure: Five-node front-facing overview: blue write entrance points to primary, primary synchronizes to two replicas; green query entrance points toward both replicas. Below it, an orange failover note with NO arrows. Only exact_text may appear; omit automatic panel captions.
